message.content:
In this repository (/bench/repo, a Go project - looks like usememos/memos), find the code that sends outbound HTTP webhook notifications to external systems when content changes (e.g. memo created/updated webhooks).

I need:
1. The exact function that performs the outbound HTTP delivery (executes the actual http.Post/http.Client.Do call) — file path and function name/line.
2. Any protection mechanism that prevents the webhook URL from targeting internal/private network addresses (SSRF protection) — e.g. validation against private IP ranges, localhost, link-local, etc. File path and function/line.

Search terms: "webhook", "Dispatch", "SendWebhook", "http.Post", "IsPrivate", "SSRF", "internal", "loopback", "private ip", "resolveWebhook", etc. Report file:line citations.

content.text:
Found the complete implementation in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/`.

## 1. Outbound HTTP delivery function

**`Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120-180`

This is the function that actually performs the HTTP call. It marshals the payload to JSON, builds the request, optionally adds an HMAC-SHA256 "Standard Webhooks" signature (`webhook-id`/`webhook-timestamp`/`webhook-signature` headers), and executes it via `safeClient.Do(req)` at **webhook.go:152**.

There's also an async wrapper, **`PostAsync`** (webhook.go:184-196), which pushes the payload onto a bounded channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128) consumed by 4 worker goroutines spun up in `init()` (webhook.go:42-55) that call `Post` in the background — this is what's actually used to fire webhooks without blocking the memo create/update request path.

## 2. SSRF protection

Two layers, both in the `internal/webhook` package:

**a) Dial-time enforcement (defense in depth, catches TOCTOU/DNS-rebinding):**
`safeDialContext(ctx, network, addr)` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`. This is installed as the `DialContext` on a custom `http.Transport` used by the package-level `safeClient` (webhook.go:32-37), so *every* webhook POST resolves the hostname and checks each resulting IP via `isReservedIP` before the socket dial actually proceeds — this defeats a "validate-then-swap-DNS" rebinding attack because the check happens at actual connection time, not just at validation time.

**b) Pre-save validation (fails fast when a webhook URL is registered):**
`ValidateURL(rawURL string) error` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62-83`. Checks the URL parses, uses http/https, resolves via `net.LookupHost`, and rejects if any resolved IP is reserved/private.

Both layers depend on the shared helper **`isReservedIP(ip net.IP) bool`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:44-54`, which checks against `reservedNetworks` (parsed from `reservedCIDRs` at validate.go:14-23): loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1/128), RFC-1918 private ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), link-local/cloud IMDS (169.254.0.0/16), IPv6 unique-local (fc00::/7), and IPv6 link-local (fe80::/10).

Note: there's an escape hatch — package-level var **`AllowPrivateIPs bool`** (validate.go:41) which, if set true, disables the SSRF check entirely (intended for self-hosted deployments targeting local-network services). Worth confirming how/where this flag gets set in production config, since it's a global toggle that fully disables the protection.

Callers that trigger these webhooks on memo create/update are in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, `memo_service_comments.go`, and `memo_update_helpers.go` (registration/validation entry points are in `user_service_webhooks.go` and `memo_service_webhooks.go`), all invoking `webhook.PostAsync` / `webhook.ValidateURL`.
